requirements.requirement: Enough eligible RRMM patients: 1-4 prior lines including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor, progressing, measurable disease, ECOG 0-1, about 410 randomized 1:1 worldwide
requirements.source: protocol.md: Key Inclusion Criteria 2-4; Phase 3, randomized 1:1, planned enrollment 410

requirements.requirement: Patients must not have had pomalidomide or elotuzumab
Patients must not have had BCMA-directed immunotherapy (BCMA ADCs are allowed)
24-hour inpatient monitoring after linvoseltamab step-up dose 1 (5 mg, Day 1) and step-up dose 2 (25 mg, Day 8); 200 mg first full dose on Day 15
requirements.source: https://www.regeneron.com/downloads/lynozyfic_fpi.pdf (Section 2.2: hospitalize 24 h after the first and second step-up doses)

requirements.requirement: Ability to recognize and treat CRS and neurologic toxicity including ICANS (boxed warning), with treatment such as tocilizumab and corticosteroids available right away

Commercial linvoseltamab is restricted under the LYNOZYFIC REMS (certified prescribers, pharmacies and healthcare settings); experience with T-cell-engager REMS shows the site can run the safety workflow

Frequent IV visits: linvoseltamab weekly Weeks 4-13, then every 2 weeks, then every 4 weeks for VGPR or better at Week 24+; elotuzumab IV weekly in cycles 1-2, then every 4 weeks, with premedication and infusion-reaction observation
Pomalidomide in the EPd arm requires the pomalidomide REMS (certified prescriber and pharmacy, pregnancy testing and contraception counseling, 28-day supply limit)
Serious infections (42% in LINKER-MM1), neutropenia and hypogammaglobulinemia: immunoglobulin monitoring, PJP and herpesvirus prophylaxis, IVIG access
Bone marrow sampling for MRD and IRC-assessed IMWG response, so marrow samples and M-protein samples must ship to central labs on time
requirements.source: protocol.md: Outcomes (MRD negative status in the bone marrow; PFS/OR by Independent Review Committee)

requirements.requirement: Processing and frozen storage of serum PK, ADA and neutralizing-antibody samples
requirements.source: protocol.md: Outcomes (concentration of linvoseltamab in serum; ADAs; NAbs)

requirements.requirement: Patient-reported outcomes at visits: BPI-SF, EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-MY20, PGIS, PGIC, EQ-5D-5L
requirements.source: protocol.md: Outcomes (BPI-SF Item 3, EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-MY20, PGIS, PGIC, EQ-5D-5L)

requirements.requirement: No local competition for the same lenalidomide/PI-exposed, BCMA-naive RRMM patients
requirements.source: protocol.md: Key Inclusion Criterion 3; Key Exclusion Criterion 6

requirements.requirement: Fast study start-up (IRB and contract) so the site enrolls within the trial's recruitment window
After each step-up dose patients must not drive for 48 hours, so they need a caregiver or transport
requirements.source: https://www.regeneron.com/downloads/lynozyfic_fpi.pdf (Section 5.2 and Patient Counseling: refrain from driving for 48 hours)

prefill_plan: Multiple myeloma trials recruiting now at the site, with phase and sponsor (ClinicalTrials.gov)
Competing BCMA bispecific, CAR-T and other RRMM trials recruiting at the site that target lenalidomide/PI-exposed patients (ClinicalTrials.gov)
Site's past MM and T-cell-engager trial history, including earlier Regeneron linvoseltamab, REGN5459 and odronextamab studies (ClinicalTrials.gov)
Named PI and sub-investigators' 1572 filing history and current institution (FDA BMIS)
PI's industry research payments by trial, showing recent bispecific trial leadership (CMS Open Payments)
PI's NPI, specialty and practice location (NPI Registry)
FACT accreditation for immune effector cell / cellular therapy (FACT public accredited-organization directory)
Authorized treatment center status for commercial BCMA CAR-T (manufacturer public treatment-center locators)
NCI cancer center designation (NCI public list)
Hospital inpatient and ICU bed counts (CMS hospital cost reports)
Research office / sponsor-facing contracting contact and published IRB of record policy (institution research-office web pages)

questionnaire.question: How many new patients with relapsed/refractory myeloma after 1-4 prior lines (including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor) does your myeloma program see per year?
Of those patients, about what percentage have never received pomalidomide?
Of those patients, about what percentage have never received a BCMA-directed bispecific or CAR-T?
How many patients could your site realistically randomize per month in this study?
Can your site admit study patients for 24-hour inpatient monitoring on a scheduled day (Day 1 and Day 8) without bed-availability delays?
Is tocilizumab stocked on the unit or in the pharmacy so it can be given within 2 hours of a CRS diagnosis, 24/7?
Does your institution have a written CRS/ICANS management policy for T-cell-engaging bispecific antibodies?
How many commercial T-cell-engager REMS programs (e.g., TECVAYLI, ELREXFIO, TALVEY, LYNOZYFIC) is your site certified in now?
Is your pharmacy certified to dispense pomalidomide under its REMS?
How many days' lead time does your infusion center typically need to book a recurring weekly infusion chair slot?
Does your site routinely give IVIG to myeloma patients receiving bispecifics when IgG is low?
Can your site ship fresh bone marrow aspirate to a central lab by overnight courier on the day of collection, Monday through Thursday?
Does your site have a monitored -70 C or colder freezer for research serum samples?
Can your staff give sponsor-provided electronic PRO tablets to patients at clinic visits?
How many trials for the same patient population (RRMM, 1-4 prior lines, BCMA-naive) do you expect to open at your site in the next 12 months that are not yet public?
What is your typical time, in weeks, from receipt of the final protocol to clinical trial agreement and budget execution for an industry Phase 3 trial?
